mainTopic: Whether חצי נזק is ממון or קנס and what that means in practice, then the new פרק on who receives the payments for a seduced נערה.
overview: The גמרא asks whether the half-damages paid by the owner of a שור תם (פלגא נזקא) is ממון or a קנס. If it were a קנס, the owner would not pay when he admits it himself. First the גמרא explains that the list of differences between תם and מועד follows רבי יוסי הגלילי. Then it tries proofs from our משנה. The 'המית שורי' proof is pushed aside because the whole משנה is about a מועד. The 'זה הכלל' proof finally works on its wording, and the view that half-damages is a קנס gets a תיובתא. Even so, the גמרא rules that the הלכה is that half-damages is a קנס, because the משנה avoided the broader wording only on account of צרורות, which is ממון. As a result, unusual damage like a dog eating lambs is not collected in בבל. Still, a victim who seizes payment keeps it, he can demand a hearing in ארץ ישראל, and the owner is put in שמתא until he removes the danger, following רבי נתן. After the הדרן, a new פרק opens with a משנה about who gets the payments for a seduced or forced נערה: the father, the brothers, or the girl herself. רבי שמעון's view continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The list of differences follows רבי יוסי הגלילי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the source listing differences between תם and מועד follows רבי יוסי הגלילי, who holds a תם also pays half the כופר. So כופר is not a missing difference.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion is this? It is רבי יוסי הגלילי, who said that the owner of a תם pays half the כופר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the earlier defense that the list of differences between תם and מועד leaves things out, with כופר as the example. The list follows רבי יוסי הגלילי, so כופר is not missing at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the חכמים, a תם that kills a person pays no כופר at all, so that would be a difference the list left out. According to רבי יוסי הגלילי, a תם pays half the כופר, just as it pays half for other damages, so nothing is missing and the list is complete. That means 'the list leaves things out' cannot explain why it does not mention that a תם is not paid on admission, so the problem for the view that חצי נזק is a קנס remains.

keyTerms.meaning: An ox not yet known to gore. Its owner pays half-damages.
Ransom paid when a known goring ox kills a person

phrases.english: Whose opinion is this?
It is Rabbi Yosei HaGelili,
who said: the owner of an innocuous ox pays half the ransom.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא מַנִּי רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the defense raised just before this amud ('תנא ושייר', with כופר as the example of something left out). The challenge to the view that חצי נזק is a קנס stands, and step 2 moves on to a new proof.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the source to a specific תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The list could be called incomplete ('תנא ושייר') because it seems to leave out the כופר difference.
steps.terutzMaskana: Following רבי יוסי הגלילי, there is no separate כופר difference, so the list is complete and 'תנא ושייר' fails as a defense.

steps.title: Proof from 'my ox killed so-and-so'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings our משנה: someone who admits 'my ox killed so-and-so' or 'killed so-and-so's ox' pays on his own admission. It suggests this is talking about a תם, which would prove that half-damages are ממון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: if someone says 'my ox killed so-and-so' or 'my ox killed so-and-so's ox,' he pays based on his own admission. Isn't this talking about a תם?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a new proof that half-damages are a regular payment and not a fine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a rule that a person who admits to something that would make him pay a קנס does not pay. If the owner of a תם pays half-damages on his own admission, then half-damages cannot be a קנס. They must be ממון.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't it? It introduces a suggested reading.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
'My ox killed so-and-so,'
or 'my ox killed the ox of so-and-so,'

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי זֶה מְשַׁלֵּם עַל פִּי עַצְמוֹ.
phrases.english: this one pays based on his own admission.
Isn't it talking about an innocuous ox?

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: הֵמִית שׁוֹרִי אֶת פְּלוֹנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After closing the previous line, the גמרא opens a new proof attempt from our משנה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Our משנה: המית שורי את פלוני או שורו של פלוני משלם על פי עצמו

steps.title: No, the case is a forewarned ox
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof: the משנה is talking about a מועד, who pays full damages.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is talking about a מועד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes the proof aside by reading the case as a מועד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מועד pays full damages, and everyone agrees that is ממון. So paying on his own admission there tells us nothing about the half-damages of a תם.

keyTerms.meaning: A forewarned ox known to gore. Its owner pays full damages.

phrases.english: No, it is talking about a forewarned ox.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the reading that the משנה is about a תם
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The case can just as easily be a מועד, which proves nothing about half-damages.

steps.title: Why didn't the משנה split the case itself?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the rejection. If a תם would not pay on admission, the משנה should have made the contrast inside the same case (מועד pays, תם doesn't) instead of moving to the case of a slave.
steps.simpleTranslation: But with a תם, what? Does he not pay on his own admission? Then instead of teaching in the last part 'if it killed so-and-so's slave, he does not pay on his own admission,' the משנה should have split the case itself: 'When is this said? With a מועד. But a תם does not pay on his own admission!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer 'it's a מועד' by asking why the משנה didn't make the more obvious contrast.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The סיפא brings a slave case, where the 30 שקלים are a קנס, to show when a person does not pay on admission. If a תם also didn't pay on admission, the easier contrast would be right inside the same ox case. The משנה didn't do that, which suggests a תם does pay on admission.

keyTerms.meaning: Instead of teaching the last part of the משנה
Let it make the distinction within the same case
When is this said? It limits a ruling.

phrases.english: But with an innocuous ox, what is the law?
Does he not pay based on his own admission?
Then instead of teaching the last part:
'My ox killed the slave of so-and-so,'
he does not pay based on his own admission,
let it distinguish and teach within the same case:
When is this said? With a forewarned ox,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל תָּם — אֵינוֹ מְשַׁלֵּם עַל פִּי עַצְמוֹ!
phrases.english: but with an innocuous ox, he does not pay based on his own admission!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל בְּתָם מַאי, אֵינוֹ מְשַׁלֵּם עַל פִּי עַצְמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rejection in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the משנה is only about a מועד
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a תם did not pay on admission, the משנה would have shown that contrast inside the ox case instead of using the slave case.

steps.title: The whole משנה is about a forewarned ox
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the entire משנה deals only with a מועד, so it never discusses a תם at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: The whole משנה is talking about a מועד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends its rejection: the משנה simply never talks about a תם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since every case in the משנה is about a מועד, including the slave case, there was no place to contrast with a תם. So this proof falls away, and the גמרא tries another one in step 6.

keyTerms.meaning: All of it, meaning the entire משנה

phrases.english: The whole משנה is speaking about a forewarned ox.

steps.whatToRemember: The 'המית שורי' proof fails because the whole משנה can be read as being only about a מועד.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה should have contrasted מועד with תם.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה never discusses a תם, so no contrast was needed.

steps.title: Proof from 'זה הכלל': paying less than the damage
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the general rule of the משנה: whoever pays more than he damaged does not pay on admission. It infers that someone who pays less, like half-damages, does pay on admission.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: this is the rule: anyone who pays more than what he damaged does not pay on his own admission. This implies that someone who pays less than what he damaged does pay on his own admission.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a third proof, this time from a דיוק (inference) in the משנה's general rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Paying more than the damage is a קנס, so it is not paid on admission. The inference suggests that paying less, like a תם's half-damages, is paid on admission. That would make it ממון.

phrases.english: Come and hear: this is the rule:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הַמְשַׁלֵּם יָתֵר עַל מַה שֶּׁהִזִּיק —
phrases.english: anyone who pays more than what he damaged
does not pay based on his own admission.
This implies: less than what he damaged
he does pay based on his own admission.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, זֶה הַכְּלָל: כׇּל הַמְשַׁלֵּם יָתֵר עַל מַה שֶּׁהִזִּיק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new proof attempt after the previous one was pushed aside.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The inference from 'זה הכלל' in our משנה

steps.title: Read it as 'exactly what he damaged'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the inference. The rule only implies that someone paying exactly what he damaged pays on admission, so it says nothing about paying less.
steps.simpleTranslation: Don't say 'this implies less than what he damaged.' Rather, say: 'this implies exactly what he damaged,' and that is paid on his own admission.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes aside the proof by changing what the rule implies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The opposite of 'more than the damage' can be 'exactly the damage', which is clearly ממון. Read this way, the rule does not cover half-damages either way. The next step challenges this reading.

keyTerms.meaning: Exactly as much as he damaged

phrases.aramaic: לָא תֵּימָא הָא פָּחוֹת מִמַּה שֶּׁהִזִּיק,
phrases.english: Do not say: this implies less than what he damaged,
rather, say:
this implies exactly what he damaged:
he pays based on his own admission.

steps.whatToRemember: The 'זה הכלל' proof is pushed aside for now by reading its inference as 'exactly what he damaged.' Step 8 challenges that reading, and step 9 ends in a תיובתא.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying a תם doesn't pay on admission. It is only saying this rule doesn't tell us either way.
steps.triggerLanguage: לָא תֵּימָא הָא פָּחוֹת מִמַּה שֶּׁהִזִּיק, אֶלָּא אֵימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference of step 6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the inference 'less than the damage'
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The opposite of 'more' can be 'exactly the damage', so half-damages are not addressed.

steps.title: Then the משנה should have used a broader rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks the rejection in step 7. If someone who pays less than the damage also does not pay on admission, the משנה should have said 'whoever does not pay exactly what he damaged,' which would cover both more and less.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about someone who pays less? Does he also not pay on his own admission? Then the משנה should have taught: 'This is the rule: anyone who does not pay exactly what he damaged does not pay on his own admission,' since that wording covers both less and more!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the rejection from step 7 and says it doesn't work. If paying less is also exempt on admission, the משנה chose the wrong wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 said the rule 'whoever pays more' only implies that someone who pays exactly the damage pays on admission. The גמרא answers that if both 'more' and 'less' were exempt, the משנה would have used one wording, 'not exactly what he damaged,' to cover both. Since the משנה said only 'more,' it suggests that paying less, like חצי נזק, does count as ממון and is paid on admission.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it teach. The משנה should have said it this way.
Exactly as much as he damaged

phrases.english: But one who pays less, what is the law?
phrases.notes: He means someone who pays less than the damage he caused, like חצי נזק.

phrases.english: Does he also not pay on his own admission?
Then let it teach: This is the rule:
Anyone who does not pay exactly what he damaged
does not pay on his own admission,
since that would include both less and more!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל פָּחוֹת מַאי, אֵינוֹ מְשַׁלֵּם עַל פִּי עַצְמוֹ? לִיתְנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rejection in step 7 and brings back the proof from step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 7 that the משנה's rule says nothing about someone who pays less.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If 'less' were also exempt, the משנה would have used a single broader wording. Since it chose the narrower 'more,' 'less' must not be exempt.

steps.title: The view that half-damages is a fine is refuted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא declares that the view that חצי נזק is a קנס has been decisively refuted.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is a conclusive refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends the argument by saying the view that חצי נזק is a קנס has been knocked down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wording argument in step 8 could not be answered. The opinion of רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע, that חצי נזק is a קנס, is therefore refuted by the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: A conclusive refutation. The view is knocked down by a source.

phrases.english: It is a conclusive refutation.
phrases.notes: This knocks down the view of רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע from earlier, that חצי נזק is a fine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Concludes that the challenge in step 8 succeeds.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: From the wording of the משנה, the view that חצי נזק is a קנס is refuted.

steps.title: The הלכה: half-damages is a fine
steps.stepSummary: Surprisingly, the גמרא rules that the הלכה is that חצי נזק is a קנס.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is: half-damages is a fine.
steps.whatsHappening: Right after the refutation, the גמרא rules like the refuted view: חצי נזק is a קנס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This looks like a contradiction, because a refuted view normally does not become the הלכה. The גמרא will question this in the next step and then explain it.

keyTerms.meaning: A fine (קנס), as opposed to ordinary money owed

steps.whyThisMatters: This ruling decides whether חצי נזק can be paid on one's own admission and whether courts in בבל can collect it.

phrases.english: And the halacha is: half-damages is a fine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a practical ruling that seems to contradict the refutation in step 9.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In practice, חצי נזק is a קנס.

steps.title: How can a refuted view be the halacha?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how a view can be both refuted and accepted as the הלכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A refutation, and also the הלכה?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out the clash between step 9 and step 10.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A תיובתא normally ends a view completely. Ruling that the הלכה follows it seems to contradict the refutation the גמרא just stated.

phrases.english: A refutation, and also the halacha?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the ruling in step 10 in light of step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that חצי נזק is a קנס.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A view that has been decisively refuted cannot also be the practical הלכה.

steps.title: The broader wording was avoided because of pebbles
steps.stepSummary: Yes, the הלכה follows that view. The refutation depended only on the משנה not saying 'exactly what he damaged.' The משנה avoided that wording because of חצי נזק צרורות, which is a received הלכה and counts as ממון, so it would have broken the broad rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes. Why was the view refuted? Because the משנה did not say 'exactly what he damaged.' But the משנה could not state that rule without exception, since there is half-damages for pebbles, which we know by tradition is a money payment. That is why it did not say it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by showing that the refutation was weaker than it looked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The broad rule 'whoever does not pay exactly what he damaged does not pay on admission' would have been wrong in one case: חצי נזק צרורות. That payment is less than the damage, yet it is ממון and is paid on admission. So the משנה had a good reason to avoid the broad wording, and its silence proves nothing about ordinary חצי נזק.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not a clean rule for him; there is an exception.
Half-damages for pebbles kicked up by an animal as it walks normally
It is a received tradition, a הלכה passed down
Ordinary money owed (ממון), not a fine

steps.confusionAlert: Both payments are 'half-damages,' but they are not the same. Ordinary חצי נזק for a תם is a קנס, while חצי נזק צרורות is ממון because of a received tradition.
steps.whatToRemember: חצי נזק of a תם is a קנס. The only reason the משנה did not state a broader rule is the exception of צרורות, which is ממון.

phrases.english: Yes.
What is the reason it was refuted?
Because it did not teach "exactly what he damaged."
But that would not have been a clean rule for him.
Since there is half-damages for pebbles,
phrases.notes: This is when an animal walking normally kicks up pebbles that break something.

phrases.english: which we know as a received halacha is a money payment,
therefore it did not teach it that way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 11 by weakening the wording proof from step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the משנה's wording by pointing to an exception that would have made the broad rule wrong.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Leaving out 'exactly what he damaged' proves that ordinary half-damages is ממון.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה left it out only because of צרורות, so ordinary חצי נזק can still be a קנס.

steps.title: Practical result: unusual animal damage is not collected in בבל
steps.stepSummary: Since חצי נזק is a קנס, damage that is unusual for an animal, like a dog eating lambs or a cat eating large roosters, is not collected in בבל. A cat eating small roosters is normal behavior, so that damage is collected.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that you said half-damages is a fine: a dog that ate lambs, or a cat that ate large roosters, is unusual, and we do not collect it in בבל. But small roosters are its normal way, and we collect.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא applies the ruling that חצי נזק is a קנס to real cases in בבל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unusual damage by a תם is paid as half-damages, which is a קנס. Courts in בבל do not have the authority to collect fines. Normal animal behavior, like eating food, falls under שן and is full ממון, so it can be collected anywhere.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the practical difference between ממון and קנס: courts outside ארץ ישראל can collect the first but not the second.

phrases.english: And now that you have said
that half-damages is a fine,
a dog that ate lambs,
and a cat that ate large roosters,
that is unusual, and we do not collect it in Babylonia.
But small ones
are its normal way, and we collect.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws practical results from the ruling in step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Unusual damage by a תם is a קנס and is not collected in בבל. Normal eating damage is ממון and is collected.

steps.title: Seizing payment and demanding a hearing in ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: Even though fines are not collected in בבל, a victim who seizes the payment keeps it. If he asks for a hearing in ארץ ישראל, the court sets one, and if the other party refuses to go, he is put in שמתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he seized, we do not take it away from him. If he said, 'Set me a time for ארץ ישראל,' we set it for him. And if the other does not go, we excommunicate him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds ways the victim can still get a fine paid, even in בבל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fine is truly owed; the courts in בבל just lack the authority to collect it. So if the victim seizes it himself, the court leaves it with him. He can also take the case to ארץ ישראל, and the court backs this by putting a refusing party in שמתא.

keyTerms.meaning: We take it away from him
Set me a time (for a court hearing)

steps.whatToRemember: In בבל, fines are not collected by the court. But a victim who seizes payment keeps it, and he can force a hearing in ארץ ישראל under threat of שמתא.

phrases.english: And if he seized it,
phrases.notes: This is the injured party, grabbing the amount of the fine on his own.

phrases.english: we do not take it away from him.
And if he said:
Set me a time to go to Eretz Yisrael,
we set it for him.
And if he does not go,
phrases.notes: This is the other side, the one who owes the fine.

phrases.english: we excommunicate him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds further practical rules about fines that cannot be collected in בבל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Seized fines are not taken back. A hearing in ארץ ישראל can be demanded, and a party who refuses is put in שמתא.

steps.title: Either way, the owner of a dangerous animal is put in שמתא
steps.stepSummary: Whether or not the damager agrees to go to ארץ ישראל, the court in בבל puts him in שמתא and tells him to remove the thing causing damage, following רבי נתן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Either way, we put him in שמתא, because we tell him: Get rid of your damaging thing. This follows רבי נתן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds to the last ruling. Even if the damager agrees to go to court in ארץ ישראל, he is still put in שמתא in בבל until he removes the dangerous animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 said שמתא is used if he refuses to go to ארץ ישראל. This step adds a second, separate reason for שמתא: keeping something dangerous at all. That reason does not depend on collecting the fine, so it applies either way.

keyTerms.meaning: We put him in שמתא (a ban)

steps.whyThisMatters: Even when a בבל court cannot collect a קנס, it can still protect people by pressuring the owner to get rid of the danger.

phrases.english: Either way
we put him in שמתא.
Because we say to him:
Remove your damaging thing,
based on רבי נתן.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּין כָּךְ וּבֵין כָּךְ מְשַׁמְּתִינַן לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, independent ground for שמתא beyond refusing to go to ארץ ישראל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The owner of a damaging thing is put in שמתא until he removes it, whether or not he agrees to go to court in ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: רבי נתן's source: do not keep dangers in your house
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי נתן: the פסוק 'ולא תשים דמים בביתך' forbids keeping a vicious dog or a shaky ladder in your house.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: רבי נתן says, from where do we know that a person may not raise a vicious dog in his house, or set up a shaky ladder in his house? Because the פסוק says: 'Do not put blood in your house.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the ברייתא of רבי נתן that it just mentioned. This is the source for telling the owner to get rid of his damaging animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק is about building a fence around a roof. רבי נתן reads it as a general ban on keeping anything dangerous at home. Since keeping a vicious dog is forbidden, a person who refuses to remove it can be put in שמתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not put blood in your house (a ban on keeping dangers at home)

phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא: רבי נתן says:
From where do we know that a person may not raise
a vicious dog in his house,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא יַעֲמִיד סוּלָּם רָעוּעַ בְּתוֹךְ בֵּיתוֹ,
phrases.english: and may not set up a shaky ladder in his house?
As it is said:
"Do not put blood in your house."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the rule in Step 15.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that the owner must remove his damaging animal, or else be put in שמתא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי נתן, reading 'ולא תשים דמים בביתך' as a ban on keeping dangers at home.
steps.whatToRemember: חצי נזק is a קנס, so unusual damage is not collected in בבל. Still, the victim keeps what he seizes, and the owner is put in שמתא until he removes the danger, because of רבי נתן's פסוק.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק אלו נערות
steps.stepSummary: The closing line for the third פרק of כתובות, אלו נערות.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק אלו נערות.
steps.whatsHappening: The פרק is over. This traditional line marks the end of פרק אלו נערות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No new law is taught here. It is a closing formula that shows we have finished the פרק and hope to come back and learn it again.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you (the closing words of a פרק)
The name of the פרק just finished

phrases.english: We will return to you, "These are the young girls"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Formally closes the פרק after the final discussion.

steps.title: New פרק: the payments for a seduced girl belong to her father
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה rules that the payments for בושת, פגם and קנס go to the father of a seduced נערה, and the same is true for צער when she was forced. If she went to court while the father was alive, the money is his, and if he then dies, it goes to her brothers.
steps.simpleTranslation: A נערה who was seduced: her shame payment, her loss-of-value payment, and her fine belong to her father. The pain payment, in a case where she was forced, also goes to him. If she went to court before the father died, the payments belong to the father. If the father then died, they belong to the brothers.
steps.whatsHappening: A new פרק opens with a משנה about who receives the payments owed for a נערה who was seduced or forced. It starts with the simple case: the father receives them, and his sons inherit them if he dies after the court case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The court case is what makes the money the father's. Once he was owed it in his lifetime, it is part of his estate, so his heirs, the brothers, receive it even if it had not yet been paid.

keyTerms.meaning: A young girl who was seduced
Payment for the drop in her value
She stood in court; the case was judged

phrases.english: A young girl who was seduced
her shame, her loss of value, and her fine
belong to her father,
and so does the pain payment for one who was forced.

phrases.aramaic: עָמְדָה בַּדִּין עַד שֶׁלֹּא מֵת הָאָב
phrases.english: If she stood in court before the father died,
they belong to the father.
If the father died,
they belong to the brothers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the new פרק after the הדרן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The payments belong to the father. If the court case happened in his lifetime, his heirs, the brothers, inherit them.

steps.title: If the father died before the court case, the money is hers
steps.stepSummary: If the father died before the court case, the payments belong to the girl herself.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she did not manage to go to court before the father died, the payments belong to her.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the opposite case from the last step. Here the father died before the court ever judged the case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the father was never awarded the money in his lifetime, it never became part of his estate. The brothers have nothing to inherit, so the girl receives it herself.

keyTerms.meaning: She did not manage in time

phrases.english: If she did not manage to stand in court
before the father died,
they belong to herself.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא הִסְפִּיקָה לַעֲמוֹד בַּדִּין עַד שֶׁמֵּת הָאָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The flip side of Step 18: the father died before the court case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the father died before the court case, the payments go to the girl and not to the brothers.

steps.title: The same timing rule applies when she becomes a בוגרת
steps.stepSummary: If she went to court before becoming a בוגרת, the money is the father's, and if he dies, the brothers inherit it. If she became a בוגרת before the court case, the money is hers.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she went to court before she became a בוגרת, the payments belong to the father. If the father then died, they belong to the brothers. If she did not manage to go to court before she became a בוגרת, they belong to herself.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה uses the same pattern for a different event: the girl growing up into a בוגרת instead of the father dying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once a girl is a בוגרת, she is no longer under her father's control. So the deciding question is the same: was the father awarded the money before that happened? If so, it is his, and it passes to his heirs. If not, it is hers.

keyTerms.meaning: She became a בוגרת, a grown woman, no longer under her father's control

phrases.english: If she stood in court before she became a grown woman,
they belong to the father,
if the father died,
they belong to the brothers.
If she did not manage to stand in court
before she became a grown woman,
they belong to herself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same court-case timing test to the girl becoming a בוגרת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A court case before בגרות makes the money the father's, and his heirs inherit it. Without a court case before בגרות, the money is hers.
steps.whatToRemember: According to the תנא קמא, the court case is the key moment. If the father was awarded the money while he was alive and she was still under his control, it is his, and the brothers inherit it. If not, it belongs to the girl.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: collection, not the court case, is what counts
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון holds that if the money was not yet collected when the father died, it belongs to the girl, even if the court case already happened.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: If she did not manage to collect before the father died, the payments belong to herself.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון disagrees with the earlier part of the משנה about when the money becomes the father's. His statement continues past the end of this text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא said a court case in the father's lifetime is enough for the brothers to inherit. רבי שמעון says the money must actually have been collected. Until then, it does not count as the father's property, so the girl keeps it.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי שמעון is not talking about a case where there was no court case at all, since everyone agrees she gets the money then. He means a case where the court already ruled, but the money had not been collected before the father died.

phrases.english: רבי שמעון says:
If she did not manage to collect
before the father died,
they belong to herself,

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: אִם לֹא הִסְפִּיקָה לִגְבּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the תנא קמא about the deciding moment: collection rather than the court case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Money that was judged but not yet collected when the father died belongs to the girl, not to the brothers.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a basic question: does a court ruling alone make money count as owned, or only actual collection? The גמרא will develop this.
